newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end mildly up despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end mildly up despite profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher on Monday as late profit-taking stripped away much of the gains at the session's outset. But brokers said the stall was temporary and would not halt the market's recent rally.
The weighted index, trading at its highest levels since 1990, soared to 10,167.31 points at the opening but lost steam in late trade, settling for a gain of 16.86 points or 0.17 percent at 10,065.76.
Turnover was heavy at T$216 billion.
Trend-setting electronics again rallied the market, gaining 1.60 percent.
"Electronics continued to reflect bullish sales expectations for the second half, especially for the computer and integrated circuit makers," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.
"But the index was stuck today because other sectors did not have the momentum to rise concurrently," Fang said.

Heavily weighted financials, which has slumped since the central bank raised two interest rates on Thursday, fell 0.97 percent prior to the government's scheduled auction of more than 400 million shares of Chiao Tung Bank this afternoon.
Chiao Tung eased T$1.50 to finish at T$80.
Brokers said they expected investors to begin shrugging off profit-taking pressure and chase higher prices on Tuesday.
"As long as bullish expectations for electronics do not disappoint, the whole market's sentiment should start to see a lift," Fang said.
Buoyed by a strong economy that posted a growth of 6.83 percent in the first quarter, Taiwan's benchmark index has soared 48 percent so far in 1997.
A 10,000-10,200 range was seen for Tuesday.
